title: Yehudah ben Dorta’i
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He lived in the time of Shemaya and Avtalyon. In Pesachim 70b it is related that he withdrew together with his son Dorta'i and settled in the south (far from Jerusalem), and said: "I am astonished at the two great ones of the generation, Shemaya and Avtalyon, who are great sages and expounders, yet did not tell Israel that the festival offering (chagigah) overrides the Sabbath"; and on account of this they withdrew. Seder HaDorot wrote: "And it appears that he was a Sadducee" — may his Master forgive him for this.

notes.text: “May his Master forgive him” is Hyman’s rebuke of Seder HaDorot’s Sadducee suggestion. The phrase ע״ז means “for this” here.
